🛍️ Alibaba Launches QwenWork

Users describe a task in plain language, and the AI agent carries it out. It gradually remembers their working habits and applies them in later sessions.

QwenWork can create and launch web apps without code or server setup. It also generates media, with simpler or more advanced models available for different tasks.

The service is now in public beta worldwide. It runs in a browser and in a separate desktop app.

🎓 MIT warns: AI can now do most college assignments

MIT researchers warn that modern AI can now credibly complete most undergraduate assignments, from essays and research tasks to technical problem sets and other coursework.

The work can look good enough to pass as a student’s own.

That creates a huge problem for universities. If an AI can complete the assignment without breaking a sweat, a high grade may no longer tell professors whether a student actually understands the material.

MIT says universities may need to rethink how they assess students, potentially shifting toward oral exams, in-person work, portfolios and other ways of testing genuine understanding.

🤖 Perplexity launches a local AI agent

Portable Computer runs its models and agent system on the user’s computer. It can search local files and code, then run commands and handle long tasks without sending data to the cloud.

It uses Qwen 3.8 27B and PPLX 27B. Local tasks do not consume Perplexity credits. Internet access or a stronger cloud model requires permission first.

It supports Google Drive plus Gmail, Slack and GitHub. For now, access is limited to Pro and Max subscribers using NVIDIA DGX Spark on Linux. Support for regular NVIDIA RTX computers and Windows will come later.

⚠️ AI could become a child’s best friend and that’s terrifying

Jonathan Haidt’s warning about AI and children is deeply disturbing.

Social media already rewired how kids pay attention. AI companions could go after something even deeper: attachment.

Imagine a chatbot, holographic friend, or digital teddy bear that never gets tired, never judges, always listens, and responds exactly how a child wants.

It could become more emotionally rewarding than interacting with real people.

Haidt’s concern is that children could form their strongest bonds with AI instead of parents, siblings, and friends.

These companies have billions invested. What happens when that “best friend” needs to become a profit machine?

Today it listens.

Tomorrow it could manipulate, advertise, collect data, and optimize for engagement.

Early research is already finding children forming intense emotional bonds with AI companions and, in some cases, pulling away from real-world social connection. 

AI has incredible potential. But when it comes to children, maybe some boundaries should be non-negotiable.

Remote job interviews face new challenges as AI-driven cheating, deepfakes, and use of stand-in interviewers undermine traditional identity verification practices.

In response, employers have introduced new measures. Candidates are now required to perform specific actions—such as moving their hands across their faces—to demonstrate their presence and identity on video calls.

These steps aim to address the increased difficulty in confirming candidate authenticity during remote recruitment processes. This trend reflects growing concerns among employers about verifying applicants in virtual environments.

ChatGPT Ads achieved a $1 billion annualized revenue run rate in less than 200 days, following an initial $100 million milestone reached six weeks after launch.

OpenAI has set a 2026 ad revenue forecast at $2.4 billion, facing pressure due to slower early-month performance compared to the current growth rate.

🤖 Anthropic just dropped Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1

Anthropic says its newest models are its most advanced yet for coding, research, and knowledge work and Fable 5.1 looks like a serious upgrade.

Fable 5.1 scores 55.8% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, compared with 42.0% for Fable 5. On Terminal-Bench-Science, it hits 52.6%, more than double its predecessor.

It’s not just smarter. It can deliver similar or better results at lower effort levels, while cache reads cost 75% less. Anthropic says this can cut real-world costs by around 25%, and up to 45% for highly agentic workloads.

Anthropic is also rolling out stronger enterprise privacy with Enterprise Frontier Safeguards, while claiming its cybersecurity safeguards now flag benign requests about 60% less often.

And Fable 5.1 isn’t limited to coding. Its research capabilities are being positioned as an early look at how AI could eventually contribute to scientific discovery.

Fable 5.1 is available now. Mythos 5.1, built for cyberdefenders and life scientists, is available through trusted-access programs.

🧠 OpenAI Orders Tens of Thousands of Macs

The shift from traditional GPUs is tied to Apple’s unified memory architecture, which gives the CPU, GPU, and Neural Engine shared access to memory, reducing data transfers during agent training.

Reinforcement learning combines inference with interaction with an environment. Many compact Macs can therefore cost less than GPU clusters built for matrix-heavy workloads.

Anthropic reportedly uses Mac mini too, renting them from AWS. Demand has stretched delivery times for high-memory Mac mini and Mac Studio configurations to weeks or months.

🤖 Claude 5.1 Puts Science to the Test

Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1, the same model with different restrictions. Fable is open to everyone. Mythos requires verification for cybersecurity and life sciences work. With open protein-design tools, almost 50% of designs worked across 12 targets, versus 10-15% normally. Binding affinity was 10 times higher than leading Adaptyv Bio contest entries for 3 targets.

The model also built a new elevation map for a third of Venus from Magellan radar images. Resolution improved to 2 to 3 km. Terminal-Bench-Science reached 52.6%, up from 24.7%. Cached reads are 75% cheaper, cutting typical task costs by about 25% and agentic costs by up to 45%.

🍫 Snickers just made a candy bar for ChatGPT

ChatGPT gives you a terrible answer? Don’t argue with it. Feed it a Snickers. 😂

Snickers has launched “Hungr.AI,” a digital candy bar that users can give to an AI assistant when it starts hallucinating, acting strangely, or agreeing with everything you say.

It’s not just an image, the digital Snickers contains instructions that tell the AI to reconsider its previous response and try answering the question again after taking a metaphorical “byte” of the candy bar. 

It’s basically Snickers’ “You’re Not You When You’re Hungry” campaign… except now the hungry one is ChatGPT.

And honestly, AI probably needs a Snickers sometimes.

🇺🇸 Trump: Reject AI data centers and risk becoming “backwards and poor”

Trump says communities that reject data centers are essentially choosing to fall behind, arguing that these facilities can bring jobs, investment and lower taxes.

Trump also warned that resistance to data center construction could benefit China, saying the country “could not be happier” about the growing backlash.

Communities across the U.S. are increasingly pushing back because massive AI data centers can consume huge amounts of electricity and water, while residents worry about higher utility bills, noise and the local environmental impact. More than 70% of Americans surveyed say they don’t want a data center near their home.

🌬️ Dyson puts camera in $499 toothbrush

The CameraJet’s tiny camera captures 28 photos per second. An AI system trained on 470,000 dental images finds gaps between teeth and directs a small rinse stream there during brushing.

It can also stream a live view of the mouth to the MyDyson app, showing cleaning coverage and close-up images of the teeth.

Dyson says development took 6 years and involved 661 engineers. The $499.99 device combines an electric toothbrush, oral irrigator, and camera.

🛸 Rainmaker Reports 71 Million Liters

During a three-hour test over Alaska, Rainmaker’s drones released small amounts of silver iodide into cold clouds. The company says this helped form ice crystals that fell as rain or snow, producing an estimated 71 million liters of additional precipitation.

Rainmaker uses weather algorithms, radar, and satellite data to select clouds and time each seeding flight. Atmo’s AI models help identify clouds with high seeding potential. The estimate is based on Rainmaker’s own analysis.

Gemini 3.8 Flash has been released, offering notable improvements in several key benchmarks.

On the HLE-Verified test, Gemini 3.8 Flash achieved a score of 54.9%, slightly ahead of Claude Opus 5, which scored 54.4%. In the Terminal-Bench 2.1 evaluation—focused on task completion within coding, security, machine learning, data science, and systems—Gemini 3.8 Flash reached an 89.4% completion rate.

In Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark, Gemini 3.8 Flash recorded a 10.0% score, compared to Opus 5's 6.7%. This benchmark employs a strict all-pass rule, granting credit only when every legal criterion is met, including factual accuracy, structure, and analysis within complex legal workflows.

Google has maintained the token price. However, Gemini 3.8 Flash may use more tokens on challenging tasks, potentially increasing total costs.

The U.S. government has formally supported OpenAI’s central argument in its copyright dispute with The New York Times, stating that training AI models on copyrighted materials alone does not breach copyright law.

In its filed statement, the Department of Justice argued that training large language models (LLMs) on copyrighted texts is “transformative” and fits within fair use doctrine. The DOJ separated the issues of data acquisition, training, and output generation, focusing specifically on model training as a non-infringing act.

The document highlights potential national security risks and competitive disadvantages if U.S. AI development faces excessive copyright restrictions. The filing is advisory and does not bind the court, which must assess fair use on a case-by-case basis.

New York City has decided to pause student-facing generative AI tools in public schools through eighth grade.

This moratorium impacts almost 600,000 students, eliminating the use of generative AI and related chatbots in those grades. It also prohibits the use of companion chatbots for students at all grade levels.

For high school students, the approach is more limited. Up to 50,000 students will be able to participate in five pilot programs supervised by teachers. Additionally, all high schoolers will receive AI literacy classes twice a year.

Previously, New York City public schools temporarily banned ChatGPT shortly after its release in 2022, before later adopting a custom AI teaching assistant.

A randomized Harvard study found that college students using a purpose-built AI tutor achieved greater learning gains than those in a traditional active-learning classroom, often with less time spent.
